.engine/operations/boot-session-start.md.why: boot-session-start is the heaviest member of the orientation family — the SessionStart pack a cold session is meant to read in full, every boot. Its length is load-bearing operator-facing content: the anti-habituation collapse rules and the repair-offer contracts in Notes, each a real behavior carrying its own tool name, loss semantics, and issue/decision reference, none redundant with another. When the 150 ceiling was set the repair set held five contracts (un-stranding, catch-up, off-main return, stranded-pull-request reconcile, branch-protection re-enable) at 121 body lines; it has since grown to ten — adding fresh-copy setup (#353), engine-mechanic product-checkout orientation (eADR-0026), half-finished-upgrade finish/undo (#594), leftover-template-license clear/keep (#471), and greenfield-intake offer/dismiss (#553). That is genuine capability growth, not the repetition issue #364 trimmed. This session first trimmed the real over-narration — the per-bullet restatements of the shared repair-offer preamble, a duplicated read-only-of-canonical-state refinement, and the anti-habituation prose — landing the file at 184 body lines, then raised the ceiling to 200 for the load-bearing remainder. The 200 ceiling is the operator's deliberate choice, set with durable headroom so the next repair contract does not force another guarded edit in a later session. It is still a ceiling, not a removal: the soft nudge fires again above 200, and this rule's hard tier still fails a malformed or reasonless override, so a dead grant cannot silently accumulate. The raise lives in this guarded rule, so it needs the operator's deliberate sign-off — the recorded-reason pattern issue #273 asked for, and the resolution of issue #460 (a recorded ceiling rather than a runbook silently sitting over budget, or its load-bearing prose shaved to fit).

.engine/operations/build-orchestration.m.why: build-orchestration is the convergence runbook — where every other system's build work is actually carried out (plan, review, integrate, submit, routine, reconcile). The 120-line operations nudge starves the one runbook that legitimately spans all of those, so it carries a raised ceiling: deliberate room to grow as the build process it documents grows, not a tight fit to today's length. Earlier moves: 200 to 215 (the consumed-review-lenses record plus the dry-run disclosure line), then 215 to 250 when issue #414 completed the plan gate against the locked design (the fast-path floor and its guardrail/schema exclusion, the proportionate progress-view checklist tier, the two-input coverage proposal, the advise-re-audit rider, the Plan-time decomposability recommendation, and the fifth step-rendering rule). Since the 250 grant the runbook has gained substantial genuine capability, each a distinct contract: the owned-product cross-repo arm for the engine-mechanic building engine-template directly (eADR-0026), the un-owned upstream escalation arm through external-contribution-submit, the recognized-automation (Dependabot) disclosed not-applicable relay, the fail-open-finding surfacing in Validation, the live-helper (MCP substrate) off-notice at submit, the build-each-slice-to-full-capability intent, the write-a-deferral-at-the-site marker rule, and the ground-truth-load-bearing-claims discipline. The trim-first pass found little genuine repetition to cut here (unlike boot-session-start): this runbook is distinct contracts, not restated ones. It removed only the one real duplication — the Notes skeleton-is-posture paragraph's restatement of the Steps intro's mechanical-hook / only-wall line — leaving 392 body lines. So this is a raise-for-growth, not a trim: the ceiling moves to 450, sized for durable headroom (the operator's directive, so a fast-growing runbook does not force another guarded edit in a session or two — its history is 250 to 392 with no intervening raise), while staying a bounded ceiling: the soft nudge fires again above 450 and the hard tier fails a malformed or reasonless override. The raise lives in this guarded rule, so changing it needs the operator's deliberate sign-off — the recorded reason issue #273 asked for.

message: An operation (a runbook under .engine/operations/) must contain, as level-2 headings in this order, Purpose, then Steps, then Done when, and it may also contain a Notes section, and no others. These sections are what make a runbook followable — what it is for, the ordered steps, and how to know it is done — so an operation that omits a required one is structurally incomplete. This check catches a broken SHAPE only: that the required sections are present, correctly ordered, and that no stray section appears. It cannot judge whether a section's content is substantive — an empty or hand-wavy section passes here and is caught instead by the operator reviewing the committed change, and whether the runbook actually tells a cold operator how to perform the procedure is the audits layer's judgment, not this check's. Length over an operation's line budget is only a soft nudge to trim, never a block; the budget is 120 by default, and a specific operation may carry a higher recorded budget in length_budget_overrides. A malformed or stale override entry — one missing its budget or recorded reason, or naming no operation — is the rule's hard tier, so a dead budget grant cannot accumulate. Add or reorder the flagged sections to match the operation template (.engine/templates/operation.md) before merging.
